ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The channel resistance of an N-channel JFET shown in the <image> is 600 \( \Omega \) when the full channel thickness \( t_{ch} \) of 10 \( \mu m \) is available for conduction. The built-in voltage of the gate \( P^+ N \) junction \( (V_{bi}) \) is -1 V. When the gate-to-source voltage \( V_{GS} \) is 0 V, the channel is depleted by 1 \( \mu m \) on each side due to the built-in voltage, and hence the thickness available for conduction is only 8 \( \mu m \).
The channel resistance when \( V_{GS} \) = 0 V is _____ \Omega.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows an N-channel JFET structure: in the middle is a channel labeled N, with Source and Drain connected on the left and right respectively; above and below the channel are P+ gate regions, and the channel thickness t_ch is marked in the figure with a vertical double arrow. The problem states that when the complete channel thickness t_ch = 10 μm all participates in conduction, the channel resistance is 600 Ω. When the material, current path length, and width remain unchanged, the JFET channel resistance is inversely proportional to the effective conducting cross-sectional area, and the effective area is directly proportional to the conducting channel thickness. Therefore the resistance is inversely proportional to the conducting thickness. When V_GS = 0 V, due to the built-in voltage, 1 μm is depleted on each of the upper and lower sides, and the actual conducting thickness is 10 - 1 - 1 = 8 μm. So R(V_GS=0) = 600 × (10/8) = 750 Ω.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the central N channel between source and drain has vertical thickness t_ch, bounded by P+ gate regions above and below. From the text, full thickness 10 um gives R_full = 600 ohm. At V_GS = 0 V, depletion removes 1 um from each side, so the conducting thickness is 8 um. Apply inverse thickness scaling: R_0 = 600 * (10/8) = 750 ohm.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the N channel is a slab between source and drain, with t_ch marked vertically and P+ gates on both sides that can deplete the top and bottom portions. Divide the full 10 um channel into ten identical 1 um conducting slices in parallel. Since all 10 slices together have resistance 600 ohm, the equivalent resistance for n active slices is proportional to 1/n. At V_GS=0 V, the built-in depletion removes one slice from the top and one from the bottom, leaving 8 slices. Therefore R = 600 * (10/8) = 750 ohm.
method.CoT_raw:
The attached image shows an N-channel JFET structure: the N channel is a horizontal slab between the Source on the left and the Drain on the right. The channel thickness t_ch is marked vertically inside the N region. P+ gate regions are placed above and below the N channel, connected to the Gate terminal, so depletion can occur from both the top and bottom sides of the channel.

Divide the full 10 μm channel thickness into ten identical 1 μm conducting slices in parallel. When all 10 slices conduct, the channel resistance is 600 Ω. Resistance is inversely proportional to the number of active parallel slices, so with only n active slices, R is proportional to 1/n. At V_GS = 0 V, the built-in depletion removes 1 μm from the top and 1 μm from the bottom, leaving 8 μm of conducting thickness, i.e. 8 active slices. Therefore R = 600 × (10/8) = 750 Ω.
